about: What the zone loop adds to the zone row (data/zones/zone1.row.json, read by src/zone/zone-rows.ts zoneFor; the row owns the spawn rows, respawnSeconds, behaviour and the hero's respawn point with downSeconds and the died line). Dom 2026-10-27 (live build, on his phone): 'once the game ends you're frozen ... it's a real-time zone like Dungeon 1, not an instant game; we are making an MMO ... with spawns and respawns.' Strategy brief docs/V3-LIVE-ZONE-BRIEF-2026-10-27.md phase 1. Open loop: nothing freezes after the kill; the hero walks on (`postKill`), the corpse lies where it fell (tappable for cuts) until the zone row's spawn stands a fresh opponent `respawnSeconds` after the kill, where the hero stands, and ragdoll.leaveCorpse() leaves the dead body beside the new one for data/physics.json corpse.keepSeconds (Physics Dev's row; no second corpse timer here). A dead hero is down for the row's `respawn.downSeconds`, then stands at the pit's mark at full health. Rematch is gone in the zone; the `flag` query turns the loop off (?postkill=v1 = the frozen end screen with Rematch). The zone row's positions are in the zone's own frame (the yard and pit are around x 190 to 235); the duel sim's arena is the pit itself, so a spawn and a respawn stand at the pit's marks (src/fight/zone-loop.ts respawnPose) until the open world draws the zone. Donors: V1 Dungeon 1 / Zone 1 (respawnSeconds per spawn row), V1 open fight (kill = toast, hero death = 2 s then a warp), Armagedom Web/src/combat.js death() (corpse kept, player keeps control).

postKill.about: roam: after the opponent dies the hero is controllable (stick, camera) and the fight camera follows him; the duel sim is stopped at the kill, the hero's walk is presentation-only. startAfterSeconds: the longest the killing blow's ceremony holds him before the stick takes over (he takes over sooner when the finisher has finished playing).

spawn.about: minDistance: metres (3.25 is the gap the pit's own marks start a fight at: the hero at z 2, the opponent at z -1.25). A new opponent never stands closer to the hero than this: a hero who walked up to the corpse (it lies at the pit's mark, where the next one stands) is stepped straight back from the mark to this distance, or, if that is outside the wall, the fight starts from the pit's own marks. There is no separate grace timer: the fighters start sheathed and the opponent waits for the hero's draw (src/fight/ai.ts), the same beat as the first fight.

world.about: Live-zone phase 1b, several bosses at their spots (src/zone/spawns.ts, wired in src/client/main.ts). The page draws one place today, the Duel pit, so a spawn row's position (the zone's frame) is drawn at position minus the centre of the zone area `pitArea` (`centre`: how far across the area, 0 to 1, the sim's circle is centred; the result is the pit's own frame, where the sim's circle is). One duel sim runs at a time: it holds the spawn the hero is nearest to (the 'held' one, standing as the live rig); the other spawns stand as frozen copies of the standing rig at their spots (no sim, no ragdoll) until the hero walks into one's aggro, which hands the sim to it. retargetMargin: metres another spawn must be nearer than the held one before the sim moves to it while nobody has engaged (no flicker at the half-way line). edgeMetres: a spot stands at least this far inside the pit's wall (src/fight/sim.ts RADIUS). minSpacing: any two spots stand at least this many metres apart (Dom 2026-10-27 'space them about two times apart': they were 3.5 m, now 6.92 m; 6.5 leaves a little room; the widest three spots fit in the 5.05 m circle less edgeMetres is 7.01 m between neighbours, so this cannot rise without a bigger pit circle, which is arena geometry in the sim and out of scope). The fight starts when the hero is inside the held spawn's aggro (data/fight.json start.auto then draws for him); a hero beyond the held spawn's leash resets it to full health at its spot; a kill starts only that spawn's respawn timer (the zone row's respawnSeconds), the others are untouched.

heroDeath.about: The hero's death fall (Strategy ruling 2026-10-27: V1's `fall` of 1.4 s, src/fight/world-rules-defs.json). When the hero dies in the zone loop he plays the rig's own Death clip across `fallSeconds` (the Death role, which the hero's 106 body carries) and holds its last frame, on the ground, until the zone row's respawn.downSeconds is over and he stands at the pit's mark (the 'You died' beat). It must fit inside downSeconds. Presentation only: the sim stays stopped at the kill. ?postkill=v1 = the frozen end screen as before (no fall).

openers.about: V1's openers (origins/zone-rows/zone1.row.json spawns.openers; world-rules firstFightSeconds 10): a zone that is not safe opens with a fight soon after the newcomer arrives. Strategy ruling 2026-10-27: auto-start stays OFF in the live zone (walk in or STRIKE); this is the gentle on-ramp. delaySeconds after the page is ready (assets loaded, the hero in control) with nobody engaged, the first `count` standing spawns of `spawns` (ids in the zone row) aggro the hero as if he had walked into their aggro: their aggro range grows to reach him (never past their own leash plus reachMetres, 2 m: the newcomer at the pit's mark stands 6 m from the yard Pitborn, just beyond its 5 m leash (the bosses were spaced about 7 m apart, #102), and that fight's leash is lifted by the same 2 m; a hero who has wandered further off is left alone) and the ordinary engagement starts (auto-draw, the boss walks up). The clock runs once per visit: any engagement, a kill or a death spends it (a hero who has fought is no newcomer; it does not re-arm after a kill or respawn). The other spawns wait for the hero's aggro as before. on:false or the link query `query`=`off` turns it off (#91: nothing until you walk). ?postkill=v1 has no zone, so no opener.
